narrative.overview: The console works like a natural-history collection. Every honeypot interaction is a catalogued specimen: an immutable event with its ID, time, place and raw evidence. Every judgement about it is a determination slip laid beside the specimen, never written over it. A rule's conclusion, an analyst's classification and an AI interpretation are three kinds of slip, styled so a reader can tell them apart at a glance.
keyCharacteristics: Determination slips (rule, analyst, AI) as the signature component
One hairline border system; no shadows doing structural work
State told in sentences, not KPI tiles
Tabular mono figures for every ID, time and count; prose in a hyperlegible sans
Honest empty, stale and unavailable states everywhere

rules.name: The Earned Red Rule
rules.body: Curator red marks only high and critical severity and the alert states confirmed malicious and error. Being in an alert, matching a rule or failing a login is never red.

rules.name: The Series Rule
rules.body: Decoy identity uses the validated categorical set in fixed order; text never takes a series colour.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Data Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks values that came from a machine. It is never decoration and never sets prose.

rules.name: The One Hairline Rule
rules.body: Every container declares its edge with a 1px hairline: never a border plus a wide soft shadow, never a side stripe, never a card in a card.

dos: Do show raw evidence as preformatted text and never as HTML; attacker strings render inert.
Do write state as sentences and empty states that say what will make data appear.
Do mark items new since the last visit with a brass dot and keep rows in place between refreshes.
Do label AI output as interpretation and keep it in its own slip.
donts: Don't use red for anything below high severity, including failed logins, rule matches and membership in an alert.
Don't build KPI-tile rows, donut charts or neon threat maps; the overview answers four questions in sentences.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow above a heading, or uppercase-track section titles.
Don't fill an empty or unavailable view with sample data or a remembered value.
Don't use monospace for prose or as a "technical" costume.
